scope: Candidate and in-use data sources for samples and sondes, true discharge/load and flow, verified upgrade and improvement metadata, historic spill feeds, and regional labels and directories for Wales, Scotland and Ireland. A metadata and licence inventory: no dataset was downloaded, no account was made and no enquiry was sent.

statuses.ready_to_integrate: Open licence that covers publishing, reachable with no account, not yet used for this purpose
statuses.needs_permission: Usable only after a licence statement, a written permission, an account, a key, a budget decision or an outside contact; each of these is Ethan's action
statuses.unavailable: Not published, refused by its terms, or not usable for publishing at all
statuses.stale_archive: Published but no longer updated, or a discontinued service
statuses.already_used: Already read by a build, a test or a research export; the entry says what is still unused

measurement_kinds.measurement: A direct measurement of the water or the event (lab sample, sensor reading, monitor start/stop)
measurement_kinds.proxy: A measured quantity that stands in for the thing of interest (ammonium for sewage, treated flow for overflow load)
measurement_kinds.model: A model or reanalysis field, not a measurement at the place
measurement_kinds.metadata: Status, plan, deadline or register information about assets, not a measurement
measurement_kinds.directory: A list of places with official labels, ratings or advice

rank_method: Rank 1 is first to work on. User benefit (a dated measurement at or near a listed swim spot, a new region's observations, or a fix to a known product gap) is weighed against implementation and data cost (licence work, account or permission, fetch size, new code). Sources that need someone else's permission rank below open ones of similar benefit, because the next step is not ours to take. Ranks are a judgement, written down so they can be argued with.

recheck.method: Page reads of publisher pages, licence pages, catalogue records and ArcGIS item metadata (WebFetch). No dataset download, no account, no enquiry, and no request to an API the site's builds poll (EA Hydrology readings, EA bathing water, Stream live feeds, Open-Meteo), because of shared-IP rate limits.
